title: Biographical Sketch On Anatoly Yakovlevitch Schneider- Nagorsky,

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I. Special Branch
REPORT
Date December 1, 37
Subject Anatoly Yakovlevitch SCHNEIDER - NAGORSKY alias Anatoly Jacob
SCHLEIDER-NAGORSKY alias Anatoly Jacob SCHLEIDER.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C Crawford.

Anatoly Yakovlevitch Schneider-Nagorsky, who at various
times has assumed the above aliases, was born in the Perm
District, Russia, into the Russian Orthodox creed, on July
16, 1887. The present whereabouts of his wife (Nee Maria
Afanassievna) is not known though she is said to have spent
last summer in Chefoo. She is reported to have applied for
a divorce from her husband. Mr. Schneider, as he is now
known, was a sapper in the Russian Imperial Army during the
war, towards the latter end of which he was attached to the
headquarters staff of the Russian forces in Harbin. Upon
his demobilization in March 1918, he set up in Harbin as a
publisher-photographer. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin
in July 1929, taking up residence at apartment 24, 103 Rue
Stanislaus Chevalier, later moving to 7 Linda Terrace; his
last known address being B.7 Rue Lofton. At the time of his
arrival in Shanghai, he possessed Chinese passport No. 3C195,
issued in Harbin on November 27, 1928, by the Special District
of Three Eastern Provinces, with Japanese Visae dated July
13, 1929. He has no relatives in Shanghai, speaks good
English with a slight accent and was registered with the
Russian Emigrants' Committee on July 13, 1929.

Towards the end of 1930, he established at 216 Szechuen
Road an enterprise known as the Isida Photo Technical Association
functioning ostensibly as "Patent Consultants, Publishers,
Advertising Consultants, Commission Agents, etc. In 1931,
he published a guide to Shanghai, entitled "The Little Blue
Book" in connection with which he sent out a series of circular
letters soliciting data for inclusion in the guide. Information
was received some years ago that Mr. Schneider was a secret

报告
日期：1937年12月1日
主题：阿纳托利·雅科夫列维奇·施奈德-纳戈尔斯基（Anatoly Yakovlevitch SCHNEIDER - NAGORSKY），化名阿纳托利·雅各布·施莱德尔-纳戈尔斯基（Anatoly Jacob SCHLEIDER-NAGORSKY），又名阿纳托利·雅各布·施莱德尔（Anatoly Jacob SCHLEIDER）。
撰写人：特别情报督察（D.S.I.）劳里尔（Laurier） 转呈人：C·克劳福德（C Crawford）。

阿纳托利·雅科夫列维奇·施奈德-纳戈尔斯基，曾不时使用上述化名，于1887年7月16日出生于俄罗斯彼尔姆地区，信奉俄罗斯东正教。其妻（婚前姓玛丽亚·阿法纳西耶夫娜，Maria Afanassievna）目前下落不明，尽管据称她去年夏天曾在芝罘度过。据报道，她已申请与丈夫离婚。施奈德先生（即他现在的称呼）在战争期间曾是俄罗斯帝国陆军的工兵，战争后期被派往哈尔滨的俄军总部参谋部。1918年3月复员后，他在哈尔滨成为一家出版商兼摄影师。他于1929年7月从哈尔滨抵达上海，初居司坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Rue Stanislaus Chevalier）103号24室，后迁至林达台（Linda Terrace）7号；其最后已知住址为洛夫顿路（Rue Lofton）B.7号。抵达上海时，他持有中国护照第3C195号，该护照由东省特别区于1928年11月27日在哈尔滨签发，并附有1929年7月13日的日本签证。他在上海无亲属，英语流利但略带口音，并于1929年7月13日在俄国侨民委员会登记。

1930年底，他在四川路216号成立了一家名为“伊西达摄影技术协会”（Isida Photo Technical Association）的企业，名义上经营“专利顾问、出版、广告顾问、佣金代理等业务”。1931年，他出版了一本名为《小蓝皮书》的上海指南，为此他发出了一系列通函，征集资料以编入该指南。数年前曾收到消息，称施奈德先生是一名秘密

Soviet Agent and correspondent to the Soviet Magazines "Ogonek"
(Glimmer) and "Krasnaia Niva" (Red Harvest) to which he sent
photographs and contributed articles on events in China. No
confirmation of his Soviet connections was, however, ever
obtained.

For the past two years Mr. Schneider has been engaged
in the physical research laboratory of the Academia Sinica
on Brenan Road.

Mr. Schneider is the inventor of an improvement for
intensifying the penetrating power of firearms. The Soviet
Government, on learning of this insisted on the surrender of
the plans and formulas of this invention and the immediate
return to the Soviet Union of the inventor, himself, who was
required to place himself and his invention at the disposal
of his country. He, however, resisted this order and applied
to the French Military for protection, and commenced to carry
an automatic pistol for which he obtained a licence from
the French Police.

The French Military authorities gave Mr. Schneider free
use of their rifle range in the French Concession for the
purpose of carrying out tests and in December 1936, Mr.
Schneider, together with Mr. C.J. Laval of the Far Eastern
Review, whom he had induced to finance the venture, proceeded
in company with Lieutenant Boudet, Liaison Officer, to Tientsin
where a demonstration was held in which the penetrating power
of the improved rifle was proved to be 150% greater than that
of the unmodified firearm against which it was tested. The
French Military authorities were favourably impressed and
forwarded the results of tests to the French War Office who,

苏联特工，同时也是苏联杂志《奥戈涅克》（Ogonek，意为“微光”）和《克拉萨亚·尼瓦》（Krasnaia Niva，意为“红色田野”）的通讯员，他曾向这些杂志发送照片并撰写关于中国事件的文章。然而，从未获得关于其苏联关系的确凿证实。

过去两年，施奈德先生一直在白利南路（Brenan Road）的中央研究院物理研究所工作。

施奈德先生是一项增强火器穿透力改进发明的发明者。苏联政府得知此事后，坚持要求交出该发明的图纸和公式，并要求发明人本人立即返回苏联，将其自身及其发明置于国家的支配之下。然而，他抵制了这一命令，并向法国军方寻求保护，开始携带一支自动手枪，并已从法国警察处获得持枪许可证。

法国军方当局允许施奈德先生在法租界内免费使用其步枪射击场进行测试。1936年12月，施奈德先生与被他说服为该 venture 提供资金的《远东评论》（Far Eastern Review）的C.J.拉瓦尔（C.J. Laval）先生一道，陪同联络官布代中尉（Lieutenant Boudet）前往天津，在那里举行了一次演示，证明改进后的步枪比与之对比测试的未改装火器的穿透力强150%。法国军方当局对此印象深刻，并将测试结果报送至法国陆军部，后者

it is believed, rejected the invention for reasons which
have not been ascertained. The principle on which the invention
is based is stated to be the law of gravity.
Since the negotiations with the French military, Mr.
Schneider has taken his invention to the British military
authorities in Shanghai, to whom he had demonstrated the
invention, particulars of which have been forwarded to the
War Office for consideration.
Mr. Schneider seems to have other inventions in hand.
He claims to have formed a revolutionary theory on the law of
gravity.
Nothing detrimental to Mr. Schneider's character has
been found in police records or in the information regarding
him which has been obtained from outside sources.

D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

据信，出于尚未查明的原因拒绝了该项发明。据称，该发明所基于的原理是万有引力定律。
在与法国军方谈判之后，施奈德先生将其发明提交给在上海的英国军事当局，并向他们展示了该发明，相关详情已报送陆军部审议。
施奈德先生似乎还有其他发明在进行中。他声称自己就万有引力定律形成了一种革命性的理论。
在警方记录或从外部来源获得的关于他的信息中，未发现任何有损施奈德先生品格的内容。
